_readme: FACTS ABOUT THE CORPUS that more than one suite has to agree on. This is
DATA for the same reason tolerance_policy.json is: a list transcribed into
python, MATLAB and the standalone scraper is three lists that drift apart,
and a name in one of them changes what an existing golden MEANS.
multiModelExamples: examples that build SEVERAL models and produce one
table per model, rather than solving one model twice. Their goldens hold
the FIRST table, because that is the model every row can reproduce. Keep
the list SHORT and justified -- adding a name here silently re-points a
pythonScriptAliases: the canonical (MATLAB) example name -> the file stem
the Python edition ships it under, for the few examples whose Python twin
was written with another spelling. Consulted by the parity suite when it
looks for the twin and by doc/latex/exdoc.py when it lifts the code into
the manual: WITHOUT it the twin is invisible, and an invisible twin is a
silent skip in the suite and a missing listing in the manual, not an error.

multiModelWhy.renv_basic: 'Compare with individual stage analysis' solves one model per environment stage, Fast then Slow. Two models, not one model twice.
multiModelWhy.tut12_random_env: as renv_basic: one model per environment stage, solved standalone after the coupled run.

multiModelWhy.cqn_threeclass_hyperl: original model, then a derived model built from it.
multiModelWhy.lcq_threehosts: original model, then a derived model built from it.
multiModelWhy.oqn_vsinks: original model, then a derived model built from it.
